newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO CALL TENDER FOR HEATING METERS SUPPLIER.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO CALL TENDER FOR HEATING METERS SUPPLIER.

text.p: Bulgaria's energy committee said on Wednesday it would hold a second tender for supplying some 10,000 heating meters to district heating firms in the country under a pilot project funded by the World Bank.
The World Bank agreed earlier this year to transfer $12 million from an existing loan to the project to supply a total of 18,000 heating meters to Bulgaria's heating plants.
The Energy Committee will use the cash from a $98 million loan extended to the construction ministry last year for the modernisation of the water system.

On Tuesday Germany's Spaner Pollux GmbH, which won the first tender, signed a contract with the energy committee for supplying some 8,000 heating meters produced by Siemens, a committee statement said.
Under the contract the German firm is due to supply the meters within a year.
The committee said Spaner Pollux's offer was worth six million marks and included a five year service guarantee.
About 17 percent of Bulgarians use central heating and the meters will help them pay for their heating according to their consumption instead of at a flat rate as they do now.

Heating prices have increased to the current $13 per gigacalory from $5 in January this year and the energy committee envisages further hikes to reach $20 per gigacalory this winter, energy officials said.
